title: Annotatio I §.III: Personal predications no help — Vorstius concrete-of-concrete vs sacramental abstract-of-abstract
pass_a_gloss: It does not help in this place to have objected personal predications, seeing that concerning them our former teacher B. Johannes Vorstius most rightly observes that in them not an abstract thing is predicated of an abstract, or — what is the same — a disparate abstract nature of a likewise disparate abstract nature, but a concrete of a concrete, whereas in our sacramental [proposition] an abstract is predicated of an abstract, body of bread, and so a disparate of a disparate.
pass_b_english: Objecting “personal” predications does not help here.
Vorstius notes that in those, a concrete is predicated of a concrete — not abstract disparate nature of abstract disparate nature.
In our sacramental saying, by contrast, abstract is predicated of abstract: body of bread, hence disparate of disparate.
source_text: Non juvat hôc loco personales objecisse praedicationes, utpote de quibus rectissimè praeceptor olim noster B. Johannes Vorstius, observat, in iis, non rem abstractam de abstracta, seu, quod idem est, disparatam naturam abstractam, de natura itidem disparata abstracta, sed concretum de concreto praedicare, cùm in sacramentali nostra, abstractum de abstracto, corpus de pane, eòque disparatum de disparato, praedicetur.
